verdict.rationale: Docs repeatedly state that Fivetran connectors 'handle schema changes... automatically' so upstream schema changes are detected and propagated without pipeline breakage, and community comments corroborate that engineers don't have to babysit third-party API/schema changes (fivetran-comm-14). However, the evidence never describes a selectable policy (e.g., block new columns, allow-only certain columns, or notify-then-apply) that lets an engineer choose how changes propagate — only generic 'automatic' handling and adjacent features like Data Blocking/Row Filtering/Custom Data Type Mapping are mentioned, none tied explicitly to schema-drift policy choice. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of configurable schema-change policies (block/allow/columns), evidence of alerting tied to schema changes specifically, and independent confirmation that engineers can choose propagation behavior rather than it being fully automatic/opaque.
